children: AMD (AMD) shares fell 0.5% in morning trading Wednesday as the chipmaker rolled out an AI assistant for engineers, adding a new software layer to its embedded computing business.

Called Ross, the tool is built to handle tasks across chip, software and board development. It can work from early design through validation, debugging and deployment, while allowing engineers to interact with AMD tools through plain-language requests.

Ross also connects with AMD's technical documentation and predefined workflows for recurring engineering tasks. AMD said the system is available now and plans to expand its capabilities with additional tools over time.

The launch comes as investors also assess fresh Wall Street views after AMD's $8.2 billion stock deal for World Labs. On Sept. 29, StoneX kept a Buy rating with a $685 target, while Stifel reiterated Buy at $635; William Blair maintained Hold without a target.
The World Labs transaction is expected to close by year-end, pending regulatory approvals.

title: AMD Stock Slides as New AI Agent Launch Fails to Lift Shares
